convoLines.text: "I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. I need help. Please."
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about The Paparazzo last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Thing' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"All right —" Austin starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Tshepiso, anyway?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my aunt, Tshepiso. Went in the Taking. She laughed like a screen door in a windstorm. Boring. Right. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"We went over this," Zanele says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on that taken person."
"That again?" Zanele sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to understand what happened. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
Zanele looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Austin sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Gladys was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I'm picking up Gladys's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
The not-knowing is a splinter. I need to get it out or it'll fester.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Zanele has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Every answer just sharpens the question. I kind of love that."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on wanting to understand what happened."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Since Gladys died... I keep expecting to see Gladys at the fire. Stupid."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"I can do foraging. Not well — well enough that nobody's died from it yet. That's my whole résumé now: nobody's died from it yet."
"Still on what you're good at, anyway."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — that foraging help, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Will you help me?"
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Meera sat with me through the worst of it — cool cloth, bitter tea, watching my breathing. I don't forget that."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"I show up. That's my part."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you're better with your hands than people expect. I've been waiting to see."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You saw it too, right? Gauntlet. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
"Still nothing on Tshepiso. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Austin — Gauntlet, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that sickness help."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
